title: Maximal representatives of rational maps into separated schemes
statement: Let $T,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $Z$ separated, meaning that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A partial map from $T$ to $Z$ is a morphism $f:V\to Z$ on a dense open subscheme $V\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Two partial maps are equivalent if their morphisms agree on a dense open subscheme of $T$ contained in both domains. A rational map $r:T\dashrightarrow Z$ is an equivalence class of partial maps. Let $D(r)$ be the union of the domains of all representatives of $r$. There exists a unique morphism $r_{\max}:D(r)\to Z$ restricting to every representative on its domain. It represents $r$. In particular each representative domain is contained in $D(r)$, and any two representatives of $r$ agree on the intersection of their domains.
